written.description: Judges an MCP server's tool definitions three ways, by YARA rule, by hosted inspection API and by asking a model, so a poisoned tool description has to clear more than one kind of reader.

alive.last_commit_message:
fix: relax litellm pin from exact to floor (#289)

* fix: relax litellm pin from exact to floor

litellm==1.93.2 was an exact pin, chosen to guarantee the
CVE-2026-84377 fix. litellm pins python-dotenv exactly too, so that
exact pin transitively forced an exact python-dotenv version on every
mcp-scanner consumer -- making mcp-scanner uninstallable alongside
anything needing a newer python-dotenv (e.g. fastmcp>=3.0, per the
issue's reported resolver failure).

Changed to litellm>=1.93.2 -- keeps the CVE fix as a guaranteed floor,
frees the resolver to pick a later litellm whose own python-dotenv
range is open.

Verified: uv lock regenerated (2-line diff), uv lock --check passes,
litellm still resolves to 1.93.2 locally. tests/ subset
(litellm/dotenv/config-related): 98 passed, 1 skipped, no change from
main.

* fix: exclude litellm releases that reintroduced GHSA-3cv6-jpf6-8222

CodeRabbit's review of #289 found that litellm>=1.93.2 alone doesn't
guarantee the CVE fix the comment claimed: the advisory
(GHSA-3cv6-jpf6-8222 / CVE-2026-84377, authenticated SSRF and
provider-credential exfiltration) was reintroduced in three later
minors and re-patched each time -- 1.94.0-1.94.2 (fixed 1.94.3), 1.95.0
(fixed 1.95.1), 1.96.0-1.96.1 (fixed 1.96.2). An open-ended floor lets
the resolver land on any of those.

Verified against the advisory directly (gh api advisories/GHSA-3cv6-jpf6-8222)
rather than just the review comment's claim. Added explicit != exclusions
for all six vulnerable releases on top of the existing >=1.93.2 floor, so
the resolver can land on 1.93.2-1.93.x, 1.94.3+, 1.95.1+, or 1.96.2+, but
never on a release the advisory lists as vulnerable.

uv lock regenerated, still resolves to 1.93.2 locally. tests/ subset
(litellm/dotenv/config-related): 98 passed, 1 skipped, unchanged.
